Though Britain and the empire emerged victorious from the Second World War, the effects of the conflict were profound, both at home and abroad. Much of Europe was ruined and occupied and for the next half century, Europe became politically divided into those who lived under the yoke of communism and the former British Empire. The Second World War had also meant the collapse of the British class system and the emergence of the working class. In Britain, the Labour party, which had been founded in 1906 and had been a party to the peace movement, now came to represent the interests of the proletariat. A wave of social unrest led by the unemployed and the unemployed youth exploded into widespread labour unrest. A wave of strikes and workers' actions led by the Communist Party began to sweep western Europe.
